data.title: Algonquin Power & Utilities Corp. Completes Sale of Ownership Stake in Chilean Utility
data.description:
Algonquin Power & Utilities Corp. (TSX/) ("AQN", "Algonquin" or the "Company") today announced that it has completed the previously announced sale of its approximately 64% ownership interest in Chilean water utility Suralis S.A. ("Suralis") to a fund managed by Toesca S.A. Administradora General de Fondos ("Toesca"). The transaction was originally announced on August 28, 2026. The transaction resulted in total proceeds of approximately $126.4 million, plus an earnout opportunity of up to $1.5 million.

“This transaction represents another important step in simplifying our portfolio and sharpening our focus on our core regulated utility businesses,” said Rod West, Chief Executive Officer of Algonquin. “Our approach to portfolio decisions remains disciplined and deliberate, with a focus on strengthening the regulated platform and supporting compelling long-term value for our stakeholders. We are grateful to the Suralis team for their commitment to customers and the communities they serve.”

Proceeds from the transaction are expected to be used for debt paydown and to facilitate capital recycling into the Company’s capital plan for 2026-2028.

About Algonquin Power & Utilities Corp. and Liberty

Algonquin Power & Utilities Corp., parent company of Liberty Utilities Co., is a diversified international generation, transmission, and distribution utility. AQN is committed to providing safe, secure, reliable, cost-effective, and sustainable energy and water solutions through its portfolio of generation, transmission, and distribution utility investments to over one million customer connections, largely in the United States and Canada. AQN's common shares, preferred shares, Series A, and preferred shares, Series D are listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange under the symbols AQN, AQN.PR.A, and AQN.PR.D, respectively. AQN's common shares and Series 2019-A subordinated notes are listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbols AQN and AQNB, respectively.

Visit AQN at www.algonquinpower.com and follow us on X.com @AQN_Utilities.

data.title: Texas federal judge fails to appear for judicial misconduct investigative hearing
data.description:
By Nate Raymond

A federal judge in Texas failed to appear on Friday before a special committee for an under-oath interview to address allegations that she had abandoned her post and likely suffers from a mental condition interfering with her ability to perform the responsibilities of her office.

A three-judge committee had earlier this month directed US District Judge Ada Brown of Dallas to appear before it to address concerns raised by two separate judicial misconduct complaints that are now pending before the 5th Circuit Judicial Council.

But after a half-hour of waiting, Chief US Circuit Judge Jennifer Walker Elrod began to bring Friday's proceedings to a close without hearing from Brown herself after the judge failed to appear as ordered.

"Judge Brown has not arrived," Elrod said, according to a transcript. "No one has appeared on behalf of Judge Brown. We have not heard from Judge Brown that she is running late, and we have been given no other reason to wait."

Brown had previously told the investigative committee she would not participate in the proceedings, claiming it would compromise an unspecified parallel investigation. Elrod said that despite being urged to reconsider, Brown had continued to not engage with the panel or submit further information.

The committee had previously warned that her failure to participate could result in the committee expanding the scope of its investigation and filing a report on its findings and recommendations without the benefit of Brown's response.

Brown, who was appointed to the US District Court for the Northern District of Texas by President Donald Trump during his first term, could not be reached for comment.

The 5th Circuit committee in an earlier order released on October 19 said it had determined Brown had "abandoned her post as a federal judge" and likely suffers from a mental condition interfering with her ability to perform the responsibilities of her office, citing "bizarre emails" and "racial insults" it said she made.

Based on those allegations, the committee on September 21 took the rare step of ordering Brown to sit for a psychiatric exam within 30 days, and the judicial council on September 29 ordered her cases to be reassigned temporarily and that no further cases be assigned to her.

The committee's members include Elrod, who initiated one of two judicial misconduct complaints against Brown; US Circuit Judge James Graves; and Chief US District Judge Alia Moses of the Western District of Texas. Others present at Friday's proceedings included Walt Green and Emma Looney of Phelps Dunbar, who are assisting the special committee.

data.title: Ananya Panday turns 28: Chand Mera Dil actor's brand value hits Rs.460.7 crore with 30 brands, check her portfolio
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 30 -- Actor Ananya Panday celebrated her 28th birthday on Friday. She has emerged as one of India's most commercially valuable young celebrities, with her brand value surging 37.8% year-on-year to Rs.460.7 crore, reported exchange4media.

According to Kroll's Celebrity Brand Valuation Report released in August 2026, Ananya Panday's brand value recorded growth. She went from No 25 to the No 19 spot on the list. Reportedly, her current portfolio of over 30 brands spans luxury fashion, beauty, FMCG, jewellery and lifestyle.

The growth came even as India's overall celebrity endorsement market experienced a slight dip. The combined valuation of the country's top 25 stars fell 3.7% to approximately Rs.19,000 crore, as per Kroll.

In April 2025, French luxury house Chanel announced Ananya Panday as its first-ever brand ambassador from and for India. She also became the first Indian face to front localised campaigns for Swarovski and Jimmy Choo.

Her other international partnerships were with Skechers India. For the popular brand, she became the first female brand ambassador, along with Beats by Dr Dre and Timex.

This year, Ananya Panday's endorsements have increasingly moved up, even going beyond conventional television commercials to interactive digital campaigns, reported the website.

Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited's brand Aurelia named her its "Chief Stylist" for its festive campaign. It was called styled by Ananya. The campaign directs consumers to an AI-enabled Virtual Try-On experience on WhatsApp. The features allow consumers to digitally test festive looks curated by the actor.

Coca-Cola India's popular beverage Limca appointed Ananya Panday as brand ambassador. She was reportedly also the "Social Media Lead" for its Feel the Taazgi campaign, which took place in April 2026.

Tanishq also featured Panday in its Festival of Diamonds campaign, conceptualised by Lintas.

In the FMCG segment, Ananya Panday features in Parle Platina's Hide & Seek "Start Your Story" campaign. For the brand campaign, she was paired with Chand Mera Dil co-star Lakshya in an episodic romantic narrative which was released as Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts.

She has also led Hindustan Unilever's TRESemme Hydra Matrix campaign alongside filmmaker Anurag Kashyap.

Her long-running partnerships included Lakme, Procter & Gamble's Gillette Venus and pet nutrition brand Drools, with which she has a four-year association.

All in all, Ananday Panday's portfolio includes a variety of brands, starting from luxury labels to mass-market ones. Despite the box office fate of her latest releases, she has become a prominent face for brands.

data.title: State Department approves $2.1B Patriot missile sale to Ukraine
data.description:
The U.S. State Department said Friday it approved the sale of as many as 500 Patriot PAC-3 missiles, as well as spare parts, logistics, and support, to Ukraine for $2.1B.

Lockheed Martin is the principal contractor for the ‌sale; in July, the U.S. Army awarded the company a contract ​worth up to $58.6B to produce ⁠Patriot interceptor missiles.

The PAC-3 is the most advanced Patriot missile; it uses "hit-to-kill" kinetic energy - colliding directly with targets at over Mach 5 - rather than a blast fragmentation warhead, featuring a dual-pulse solid rocket motor and larger fins for extended range and maneuverability against ballistic and hypersonic threats, according to the Lockheed Martin website.

Ukraine will pay for the Patriot order with "donations from Canada, Germany, and Norway via the JUMPSTART program and national funds, financed by the European Union’s Ukraine Support Loan," and no U.S. funds are involved in the sale, the State Department said.

Ukraine's President ​Zelenskyy said earlier this week that his country had been waiting for nearly a month ​for the U.S. to sign off on critical missile supplies, as Russia stepped up attacks on energy and civilian infrastructure.

data.title: Nasdaq tanks 5% in October as tech bloodbath deepens
data.description:
The Nasdaq Composite Index plummeted nearly 3% on Friday amid a wider selloff in the technology sector, intensified by Intel’s weak third-quarter results.

The tech-heavy index closed 2.86% lower at 25,437 points, recording its worst single-day performance since June.

Intel’s shares nosedived during Friday’s trading session, closing 29.38% lower after its Q3 results showed guidance that missed Wall Street estimates by a considerable margin. Its peers Sandisk and Qualcomm also took a hit, ending 13.42% and 11.12% lower, respectively.

For the week, Nasdaq slumped 2.79%, while for the month, it tanked 5.30%.

The index closed lower in 11 of October’s 21 trading sessions, capping a volatile month that began with the Nasdaq notching record highs. Investor sentiment swung between concerns over rising AI capital expenditure and optimism following the Federal Reserve’s dovish stance on interest rates. Meanwhile, intermittent selling across the tech sector intensified towards month-end following disappointing results from Big Tech companies like Alphabet (GGOG) and Amazon .

data.title: The Week the Cracks in the AI Trade Grew Deeper — WSJ
data.description:
By David Uberti and Hannah Erin Lang

Slowing growth. Dwindling cash piles. Cannibalized business lines. Pressure points are multiplying across the artificial-intelligence boom that has propelled markets and the economy.

The cracks in the AI trade multiplied through the week, culminating in a sharp tech selloff Friday that sent the Nasdaq composite to its worst day since June and its worst month in more than a year.

The vulnerabilities in Wall Street's favorite trade have been building for months, periodically appearing around smaller companies drowning in debt. Each time, the largest firms behind America's AI build-out have reassured Wall Street by printing profits, suggesting the show will go on even in a world of higher interest rates.

This week was different. After tech stocks had treaded water for weeks, AI giant Anthropic momentarily rejuvenated investors with a filing that showed soaring revenue ahead of its planned initial public offering. But then publicly traded tech firms reported earnings — and markets got a reality check.

First came a dissatisfying quarterly report from Alphabet, which showed that growth in Google's search-advertising business slowed — in part because of the impact of "AI mode" queries. Traders punished the stock with a 13% decline Thursday that marked its worst day on record, hammering major Alphabet shareholders such as Berkshire Hathaway.

Then the bad tech vibes got worse. Late Thursday, Amazon reported plunging free cash flow and revenue that missed analyst estimates. American chipmaking giant Intel forecast a prolonged slowdown in personal-computer sales, pressured by memory chip prices sent skyrocketing by the AI boom.

Intel shares on Friday crashed about 30%, the worst session on record for a company that has traded on the U.S. stock market for decades. The plunge vaporized more than $15 billion in combined paper holdings by two of the company's largest shareholders: the U.S. government and Nvidia.

Write to David Uberti at david.uberti@wsj.com and Hannah Erin Lang at hannaherin.lang@wsj.com

data.title: In a wild October for markets, these stocks were the biggest winners and losers
data.description:
By Philip van Doorn

Many Big Tech stocks were hit hard but the S&P 500 showed strength under the surface, with a majority of stocks showing gains for the month

Intel was the worst-performing stock in the S&P 500 during October with a 43.5% decline, while Alphabet was down 18.5%.

October has seen a lot of carnage in tech stocks, but you might not guess that from the S&P 500's performance.

The S&P 500 SPX was down 0.5% for October through Friday morning, even though 75% of stocks in the large-cap benchmark index were up for the month.

The S&P 500 is about 40% concentrated in its largest 10 stocks by market capitalization. Meanwhile, the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF RSP was up 5.5% for October - reflecting the underlying strength in stocks, even as many of the largest technology companies have fared poorly as investors question the AI infrastructure build-out. Among the largest 10 components of the S&P 500, Nvidia (NVDA) (the largest of all) was down 8.7% for October, while Alphabet (GOOGL) (GOOG) was down 18.5%, Amazon.com (AMZN) was down 6.9%, Broadcom (AVGO) was down 5.6%, Meta Platforms (META) was down 14.7% and Micron Technology (MU) was down 16.8%. Rounding out the largest 10 components of the index, Apple (AAPL) was up 4.2% for October through early trading Friday, while Microsoft (MSFT) was up 1.8% for the month, Tesla (TSLA) was up 10.5% and Eli Lilly (LLY) soared 23.5%.

data.title: Congo Ebola outbreak kills more than 5,000
data.description:
The death toll from the Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 5,000, government data showed on Friday, as authorities had yet to find a way to control the country's deadliest Ebola epidemic on record.

There are no approved treatments or vaccines to combat the rare Bundibugyo species, which is behind the outbreak in the Central African country.

It has infected more than 10,000 people since it was declared in May.

Delayed detection, conflict and strained health services have helped the virus spread more rapidly than in previous outbreaks.

Eight of Congo's 26 provinces have been affected, with many deaths occurring outside treatment centres.

This year's outbreak is the world's second-largest ever, behind only the 2014-2016 one that infected over 28,600 people and killed more than 11,000 across ​Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone.

Last week Nigeria became the fourth African country to report an Ebola case, extending the outbreak's geographic spread to West Africa. East African countries Kenya and Uganda have also reported cases.

data.title: CME cattle futures close lower as cash market cools; lean hogs lower
data.description:
By P.J. Huffstutter

Cattle futures on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) closed sharply lower on Friday, with the most-active December live cattle contract sliding for the fourth straight session, as cash market prices softened and fund investors looked to liquidate their positions, market analysts said.

Trades in the cash cattle markets have been somewhat sluggish, and prices have also cooled, market analysts said. Dressed purchases in Nebraska were down at least $4 per cwt from last week and down $2 to $5 per cwt in other Midwestern markets.

CME December live cattle settled down 5.350 cents at 220.950 cents per pound — the contract's lowest price since October 6. Meanwhile, February ended down 5.275 cents at 224.200 cents per pound.

Meanwhile, CME feeder cattle contracts have been seeing more volatility recently, as more investors are trading in the cattle market, analysts said. CME January feeders finished the day down 10.175 cents at 331.775 cents per pound.

CME lean hog futures also turned lower, with both the February and April 2027 contracts setting fresh lows, on seasonal pressure, plentiful hog supplies, weak cash prices and slumping wholesale pork prices.

"This is a cash-led bear market," said Don Roose, president of Iowa-based U.S. Commodities.

CME December lean hog futures (LHZ26) settled down 0.95 cent at 58.875 cents per pound, and notched a weekly loss for the fourth consecutive week. February hog futures (LHG27) ended 0.975 cent lower at 63.75 cents per pound on Friday.

The CME's Lean Hog Index (.IHX), a two-day weighted average of cash hog prices, was last quoted at 67.30 cents per pound, its lowest value since January 2024. The US Department of Agriculture priced pork carcasses on Friday afternoon at $70.10 per hundredweight, down 59 cents from Thursday, though bellies firmed $7.19 at $72.85 per cwt.

data.title: Pioneer Bancorp Reports $85,000 Third-Quarter Net Income
data.description:
Pioneer Bancorp reported net income of $85,000, or approximately $0.00 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2026, compared with $4.3 million, or $0.18 per diluted share, a year earlier. Net interest income rose 16.9% to $23.6 million, while results included $6.2 million in litigation-related expense. For the first nine months of 2026, net income was $8.9 million, or $0.36 per diluted share.

Financial Highlights

  • Third-quarter net interest income was $23.6 million, up 16.9% from $20.2 million a year earlier. For the first nine months, it increased 14.1% to $67.2 million.
  • Third-quarter noninterest income increased 44.3% to $5.5 million. Nine-month noninterest income rose 20.1% to $14.8 million.
  • Net income for the third quarter was $85,000, compared with $4.3 million in the prior-year quarter. Nine-month net income was $8.9 million, down from $16.5 million.
  • Third-quarter basic and diluted earnings per share were approximately $0.00, compared with $0.18 for the same period in 2025. Nine-month basic and diluted EPS were $0.37 and $0.36, respectively.
  • Third-quarter noninterest expense rose 57.4% to $27.7 million, including $6.2 million in litigation-related expense. The provision for credit losses was $1.3 million.

Business Highlights

  • Pioneer and its bank subsidiary reached agreements in principle to resolve claims brought by Southwestern Payroll Services, Granite Solutions Groupe and National Payment Corp. The resolutions remain subject to definitive agreements and dismissal filings.
  • The April acquisition of Targeted Lending expanded Pioneer’s equipment-finance platform, which provides financing nationwide to small and midsized businesses.
  • Pioneer cited continued loan portfolio expansion and growth in its diversified deposit base during the quarter, alongside active management of funding costs.
  • The company’s financial services include banking, insurance, employee benefits, human resources consulting, college advising, wealth management and municipal bond trading.

data.title: Accendra Health Disclosed Failure to Satisfy a Continued Listing Rule or Standard
data.description:

Its listing is not immediately affected; the company has 45 days to submit a plan to regain compliance within 18 months, subject to NYSE review.
